name: Warm Pink
lede: Warm Pink is a descriptive name for a pink that leans toward red; the name is recent, but warm pinks go back to coral powder and Titian's rainbows.

sections.title: A modifier name
sections.body: The name pairs a temperature word with a basic color word, and the library's only source is the xkcd color survey of 2010 [1]. The closest ISCC-NBS category is deep pink, about 6 units away [1]. Near neighbors are [[rosy-pink]], [[fiery-rose]] and [[blush]], all within about five units [2].

sections.title: Warm pinks before the name
sections.body: Pigment books link a warm pink to coral: the tones come from slow-growing red precious corals of the western Pacific, species *Corallium japonicum* and *C. secundum*, and Japanese art suppliers have sold the ground coral as *sango matsu* [3]. In painting, Gage observes that Titian's rainbows were mostly warm, starting and ending with warm pinks and purples, in *Venus and Adonis* and *Diana and Callisto* [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1% of its canvas, within a distance of 4 units, as photographed [5]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole, and photographs of varnished paintings are not pigment tests.
